items.quote: So far capacity utilization is concerned, we are at this moment with the addition of capex is around 56% to 60% utilization is there.

items.statement: Gear Division Q4 FY26 product mix: 55% catalogue (standard) products, 45% engineered (customized) products; full year FY26 same mix.
items.quote: So, the mix of engineered versus catalogue is -- for the quarter CP is 55%, that is the standard product, and engineered product is 45%, that is the customized product. And for the year FY '26, catalogue product is 55% versus engineered product being 45%.

items.statement: Engineered products carry better margins than catalogue products; margin impact in FY26 due to inability to invoice engineered product orders.
items.quote: So, yes, we had done, the catalogue products 55% and engineered products 45%. We have better margins in the engineered products. But this year, we could not execute the order, or we couldn’t supply/dispatch the orders to the customers because of the customers' requirements. So, the margins are not reflecting in our financials

items.statement: Domestic markets contributed 82% of consolidated revenue in Q4 FY26; international markets 18%.
items.quote: Domestic markets contributed almost 82% of the consolidated revenue, while international markets accounted for 18%.

items.statement: US exports face 50% tariff under Section 232; Mexico subsidiary established to serve Latin America without that tariff.
items.quote: So, right now in the USA, we have the 50% tariff. Whatever we are exporting from India to our subsidiaries in USA or to customers in USA. So that is 50% because of Section 2(32), but with the establishment of this Mexico we will have the Latin America and that tariff is not applicable there.

items.statement: No significant capex planned for Mexico subsidiary at present.
items.quote: Not much right now. We just established. We will come back to you after some time.

items.statement: Receivables increased by ~INR90 crores YoY; INR70-75 crores due to Feb-March sales not yet due, ~INR15 crores overdue but collecting in April.
items.quote: The increase of about INR90 crores compared to last year's balance sheet if you look at it. From INR90 crores, INR70 crores to INR75 crores is largely because of the sale which has happened in the February and in the March, which has not due even as on 31st March. And about INR15-odd crores is overdue compared to the same bucket of the last year, which is getting the effect in the month of April.

items.statement: Net cash balance of approximately INR700 crores provides strategic flexibility.
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, we continue to maintain a strong financial position, with a net cash balance of approximately INR700 crores.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR1.50 per equity share (face value INR1) for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: The Board has recommended a final dividend of INR1.50 that is INR1.5 per equity share having a face value of INR1 each, which is subject to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: New CFO Chintan Shah joined with nearly 19 years of experience.
items.quote: we would like to welcome our CFO, Mr. Chintan Shah, who joined us recently. He brings nearly 19 years of experience and we are confident that he will play an important role in driving Elecon's continued growth.

items.statement: MHE Division inquiry pipeline exceeds INR1,000 crores across various sectors.
items.quote: If I am quantifying, it is more than INR1,000 crores inquiry we have right now for various sectors.

items.statement: Gear Division received LOI for single largest ever order in industrial gear business from power sector; expected to convert in 1-2 days.
items.quote: We have already got the LOI. So, it's a very single largest big order ever got in the industrial gear business market. So that is, in few days, you will get the good news. Ashwani Sharma: Okay. Dipak Dalwadi: From the power sector

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 25%-30% CAGR medium to long term, with 35%-40% aspiration for FY27
items.quote: On a medium to long term, our AUM growth guidance i s 25% to 30%. But if I were to dissect it between FY’27 and years further, I think 35% to 40% is the guidance which we are aspiring to achieve as a growth in FY’27

items.statement: PAT growth guidance of 30%-35% CAGR on previous full financial year PAT
items.quote: Future PAT guidance is on the PAT of previous fina ncial year and not on exit run rate of Q4

items.statement: ROA target range of 4.5%-5%, ROE target range of 14%-16%, cost-to-income target range of 13%-17%
items.quote: On Profitability, we shall operate with return on asset of 4.5% to 5% kind of a range, with return on equity of 14% to 16% kind of a range, and cost to income between 13% to 17%.

items.statement: NPA guidance maintained at nil; accumulated provisions of INR 18 crores as per Ind AS ECL and RBI guidelines
items.quote: our ph ilosophy and theory is very simple: we don't want to lose even INR1 in the market. So I don't wa nt to give any message that I am okay, tolerable to lose some money. By design, by target, we are not going to lose money. So that’s why our guidance is NIL NPA

items.statement: Loan book at all-time high of INR 3,936 crores, up 75% YoY; gross disbursements crossed INR 25,000 crores for full year
items.quote: We did operating income of INR 334 crores, year-on-year growth of 96%, achieved Loan Book of INR 3,936 cror es, year-on-year growth of 75% and Profit after tax was INR 128 crores, year-on-year growth of 58

items.statement: Factoring book outstanding at INR 175 crores as of March 31; TReDS onboarding completed on RXIL and M1xchange, going live in Q1
items.quote: If you look at our results closely, INR 175 crores is the factoring book outstanding on 31st March. On the TReDS, we have already onboarded two TReDS p latforms, RXIL and M1xchange. We are evaluating the leads and soon we will go live in terms of booking TReDS factoring

items.statement: ROA breakdown: NII ~7% of average AUM, total income including fees ~7.5%, cost-to-income below 15%, resulting in 4.8% ROA
items.quote: our NII is around 7% of average A UM and total income, including fees, would be around 7.5%. With Cost to Income of below 15% and then taxes, our return on asset is 4.8

items.statement: Current leverage at 1.9x (approx 2x); comfortable range 2x-3x, aspiring to reach 3x over 2-3 years; bank lines between INR 3,000-3,500 crores
items.quote: Currently our leverage is 1.9, broadly let's say 2 x. And our comfortable range is 2x - 3x with aspiration to achieve 3x over the next two to three years

items.statement: Internal target of INR 10,000 crores AUM in 3-4 years without fresh equity, using accumulated profits and existing bank lines at 3x leverage
items.quote: INR 10,000 crores is our internal target. INR 10,0 00 crores of AUM we can easily reach in three to four years without being dependent on any fresh equity, because we will accumulate profits also and there is a enough bank lines available and more bank lines will get added

items.statement: INR 21 crores incremental warrants converted in April; equity pool at INR 1,481 crores
items.quote: We are currently sitting with a INR 1,481 crores equity, added INR 21 crores incremental warrants got converted in the month of April.

items.statement: No new TReDS platform planned; will participate on existing RBI-licensed platforms RXIL and M1xchange
items.quote: No, no. We don't plan to have TReDS platform. We w ill only participate on existing TReDS regulated entities licensed by RBI

items.statement: Operating across 30 hub locations pan-India, each covering ~100 km radius
items.quote: We are currently catering to 30 locations pan-Indi a, but those 30 locations are like hubs. From a particular hub location, we cover around 100

items.statement: Business 100% domestic, no import-export financing; no direct or indirect impact from geopolitical situation
items.quote: Number o ne, our business is 100% domestic so there is no direct impact on our business. We are not doi ng any import-export financing. However, we are vigilant. We did prognosis of our portfolio in light of the ongoing geopolitical situation and there is no indirect impact

items.statement: Employee benefit expense increase of INR 1.5 crores in current quarter; previous INR 2.5 crores ESOP charge related to prior year
items.quote: No, Kushal, the INR 2.5 crores which you referred was not related to this financial year, it was previous year. If you read, this INR 2.5 crores is mentioned as a footnote, is related to period ended March 31 st 2025

items.statement: No stress seen in top sectors currently, but vigilant on potential geopolitical impact; engaging borrowers and anchors
items.quote: No, we are not seeing any stress as of today, but we are not ignoring the fact that there can be a potential stress due to ongoing geopolitical issue and we are engaging our borrowers, our anchors and we are vigilant.

items.statement: Believes in co-existence not competition; 5-6 private banks and couple of NBFCs with INR 10,000-15,000 crores AUM each in dealer finance; total market >INR 1 lakh crore including PSU banks
items.quote: Broadly five-six Private Banks and a couple of NBF Cs are operating in this space, each one dealing with AUM of INR 10,000 crores to INR 15,000 crores range in a dealer finance space. So this is my market insight. But the overall marke t, if I were to add PSU banks, I think the market size would be somewhere upward of INR 1 lakh crore

items.statement: Average churn cycle 45 days; Q4 disbursements ~INR 7,700 crores against book of INR 3,900 crores
items.quote: Our average churn cycle is 45 days. If you look at our disbursement done in Q4 versus our book, we would have done a disbursement around INR 7,700 crores against our book of INR 3,900 crores, which signifies that we have churned the entire book in 45 days on an average basis.

items.statement: Scalability huge: only 25%-30% of anchor sales covered under organized supply chain; <100 of top 500 corporates active in supply chain; no saturation for 10-15 years
items.quote: In my understanding, basis back of the hand calcula tion, only 25% to 30% of their sales is covered under organised supply chain programs. Still there is a lot of room left for those anchors to also deep dive and get their dealers onboarded u nder the organized supply chain programs. So the space is humongous. There is no saturation I see in my sight, at least for next 10-15 years

items.statement: New businesses (beyond supply chain) subject to regulatory approvals, business plan, and hiring; timing uncertain for FY27 or FY28
items.quote: Kushal, lot of groundwork is going on, because the se new businesses are subject to regulatory approvals. It has to also pass the muster of business plan. We also need to have right set of people to run these businesses. So it is subject to many t hings. So difficult for me to really visualize whether it will happen in FY27 or '28, because it's subject to many things

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of INR54 per share, payout ratio 81% subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: Board earlier today recommended a dividend of INR54 per share compared to INR45 per share adjusted for bonus issuance last year. That translates to a payout ratio of 81%, of course, this is subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: Industry saw 14th consecutive year of positive net inflows at INR7.4 trillion, equity funds INR4.9 trillion
items.quote: For the full year, the industry across asset classes saw healthy net inflows of INR7.4 trillion. Equity -oriented funds continued to be the primary driver, contributing close to INR4.9 trillion.

items.statement: Industry SIP flows hit all-time high of INR321 billion in March 2026, up 24% YoY with 97 million accounts
items.quote: In March 2026, monthly SIP collections touched an all -time high of INR321 billion, up 24% year -on-year, with 97 million contributing accounts.

items.statement: QAAUM grew 20% YoY to INR9.3 trillion, equity AUM reached INR6 trillion
items.quote: Overall QAAUM grew by 20% year -on-year to r each INR9.3 trillion, while equity -oriented AUM reached INR6 trillion.

items.statement: SIP and STP flows INR48.8 billion in March 2026, up 33% YoY; total accounts 30 million, unique investors 16.7 million
items.quote: SIP and STP flows together stood at INR48.8 billion in March of 2026, growing by 33% year-on-year. Our total accounts crossed 30 million, and unique investors with us are now at 16.7 mi llion, an addition of 3.5 million over the year.

items.statement: Direct plans now 31% of equity AUM; digital transactions 97% vs 81% three years ago
items.quote: In terms of mix, direct plans continue to gain traction and now account for about 31% of our equity AUM. Digital adoption remains very strong, with 97% of our transactions being digital.

items.statement: Launched 7 new mutual fund schemes; private credit fund first close with IFC; 2 inbound funds in GIFT City; won EPFO and SPFO PMS mandates
items.quote: During the year, we further strengthened our mutual fund offerings with launch of seven new schemes. Beyond mutual funds, we also made goo d progress in expanding our alternatives business with announcement of first close of our private credit fund with IFC as a partner and anchor investor.

items.statement: Total revenue INR46.2 billion, operating profit INR32.1 billion, operating margin 35 bps of AUM, PAT INR28.6 billion up 16%
items.quote: Total revenue for the year was INR46.2 billion, with revenue from operations at INR41.2 billion, growth of 18% year-on-year. Total expenses were INR9.1 billion. Operating profit for the year came in at INR32.1 billion, a Y-o-Y growth of 18% with an operating margin at 35 basis points of AUM.

items.statement: Equity yield 56 bps (60-61 bps active), debt 28 bps, liquid 13 bps, blended 45 bps; yields flat QoQ
items.quote: On the yields for the different classes, equity was around 56 basis points, debt 28 and liquid 13. And blended for the year was 45. There is actually no yield compression in the quarter.

items.statement: TER changes: gross impact 3-4 bps on existing book, targeted to offset via commission optimization; 5 bps exit load removal on new flows
items.quote: So, starting with the existing book, for us the gross impact is about 3 to 4 basis points and our approach is to largely offset this through optimization of commission structures, along with prudent management o f both the direct as well as indirect costs.

items.statement: Employee cost ex-ESOPs grew 12.5% YoY, 13% 5-year CAGR; headcount 1,250 to 1,700; non-employee cost 13.5% 5-year CAGR
items.quote: On the employee cost front, excluding ESOPs, our cost has grown by about 12.5% year-on-year. And if you take this over the last five years, the CAGR for employee cost, again ex -ESOPs non-cash charge, is around 13%.

items.statement: No specific expense guidance for FY27/28; costs to grow broadly in line with business and investments in technology and people
items.quote: While we don't give specific guidance, these will broadly grow in line with the business and the investments we are making across technology and people.

items.statement: Unique investor base 16.7 million, added 3.5 million in FY26 vs industry 7.2 million; penetration 27% vs 17.6% three years ago
items.quote: Our total accounts crossed 30 million, and unique investors with us are now at 16.7 mi llion, an addition of 3.5 million over the year. To put that in context, industry as a whole added 7.2 million.

items.statement: Flow share higher than book share across channels including fintech; folios grew from 2.3 crore to 3 crore
items.quote: our flow share thro ugh the fintech channel is also higher than the book share. So that reflects, I think a strong presence on their platforms. Our folios also, I think this year we have moved up from 2.3 crores folios to 3 crores folios

items.statement: Market share ~12.8-13%; aspiration to grow share but focus on expanding overall market; industry equity flows INR9 lakh crore last 2 years
items.quote: If I remember correctly, I think in the early part of last decade it would have been 20%, but of course the overall size of the market was small, incremental flows were like a small fraction of what we get now.

items.statement: New BER framework effective April 1, 2026; GST moved outside TER; 5 bps exit load commission removed; early days to quantify precise P&L impact
items.quote: So, we have a new terminology in the industry now, it's called BER, the Base Expense Ratio. It is still early days, and you will hear more from us over time on how we propose to deal with the impact, including changes in distribution commission, our margins and the overall impact on the ecosystem.

items.statement: Board approved Rajan Anandan as invitee/external expert on Technology Committee for 3 years; ex-Google India MD, Peak XV Partners
items.quote: We have announced today that Board has approved the appointme nt of Mr. Rajan Anandan as an invitee and external expert on the Technology Committee for a three -year term. Mr. Anandan is the currently a Managing Director at Peak XV Partners, who brings a deep global technology leadership experience.

items.statement: Industry SIP contributing accounts grew from 81 million to 97.2 million in FY26; B30 locations >40% of SIP flows
items.quote: At the beginning of the year, there were 81 million SIP contributing accounts that AMFI publishes and that number closed at 97.2 million as of March 26. So, there is an increase of 16 million accounts.

items.statement: Investor behaviour mature during volatility but untested for prolonged downturn; SIP flows sticky, lumpsum flows variable
items.quote: I would still say I mean on the, on the cautionary note that we have to see the investor behaviour if markets stand under pressure for a much lo nger period.

items.statement: AIF/PMS yields: alternatives marginal premium to equity margins; discretionary PMS in line with equity; EPFO/SPFO mandates tight economics
items.quote: On the alternative business, marginal premium to our equity margins. On the PMS side, pure discretionary is in lin e with equity margins. The non -discretionary, particularly the EPFO and SPFO kind, these are Government of India mandates and among the most prestigious and very tightly contested opportunities.

items.statement: SIF approvals secured; launching differentiated products thoughtfully, not a race; strategic not immediate impact
items.quote: On your question on SIF, so we have secured all necessary regulatory approvals. From our standpoint, getting the approval is just the starting point. Real question is, how do we participate in a way that is consistent with our philosophy?

items.statement: Balance sheet equity investments largely skin-in-the-game; debt portfolio passive with reasonable duration; other income impacted by Q4 market correction
items.quote: The equity investment in mutual funds that we have on the balance sheet is largely due to the skin in the game circular from SEBI. So that portion of the equity investments saw a drawdown because of the market correction in the Q4, right.

items.statement: Employee costs including ESOP expected to remain flat at ~₹11 billion in FY27 vs FY26
items.quote: So, Swarnabha, on the employee cost, we will likely be within the same range of the FY 2026 number, which is about ₹11 billion, including the ESOP cost.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin improved to 44.4% in Q4 FY26; management expects further margin expansion in FY27 but declines to give a specific number
items.quote: Importantly, adjusting for one -time items and IPL -related spend, normalized EB DAT margin improved by 498 basis points sequentially to 44.4%, reinforcing the scalability and operating leverage embedded in the platform.

items.statement: Operating margin drag from newer businesses expected at 2.5-3% for FY27, similar to FY26
items.quote: I think for the current year we will have in the range bound of about 2.5 to 3%. So that's going to be there as it was in the last year.

items.statement: Wealth management business expected to break even in 3-3.5 years; further investment planned given strong growth
items.quote: Our belief is our wealth business, for instance, is going to achieve a breakeven in about 3- 3.5 years is something that we've already indicated to the street.

items.statement: Average daily orders recovered from 5 million in Feb'25 to 7.4 million in Mar'26; aggregate quarterly orders hit 431 million, a six-quarter high
items.quote: Average daily orders scaled from 5 million in February '25 to 7.4 million in March '26, thus taking the aggregate order count to 431 million for the quarter, marking a six-quarter high.

items.statement: Retail equity turnover market share at 20.4%, up 46 bps YoY; demat market share at 16.7%, up 54 bps YoY
items.quote: We sustained a 20.4% share of overall retail equity tur nover, an expansion of 46 bps year-over-year, and further strengthened our demat market share to 16.7%, higher by 54 bps year-over-year.

items.statement: Lifetime cumulative credit disbursements reached ₹27.1 billion with ₹6.1 billion disbursed in Q4 FY26
items.quote: In credit, our lifetime cumulative disbursements reached ₹ 27.1 billion, with ₹ 6.1 billion disbursed during the quarter, reflecting steady traction.

items.statement: Ionic Wealth AUM crossed ₹100 billion, up 23% QoQ; client base 1,900+ with >45% from non-metros
items.quote: Ionic Wealth's AUM crossed ₹ 100 billion, higher by 23% quarter -over-quarter. The already strong UHNI business has evolved into a powerful flywheel, driving 2x growth over the last 12 months and enabling entry into larger and more discerning families.

items.statement: AMC period-ending AUM at ₹3.6 billion, lower sequentially; folio count up 28% QoQ to 246,000+ across 17,575 PIN codes
items.quote: Period ending AUM at ₹ 3.6 billion was lower sequentially, impacted by softer market conditions and some redemptions in the liquid fund. Interestingly, we saw our folio count increase by 28% sequentially to over 246,000 across 17,575 PIN codes.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin expanded 227 bps QoQ to 41.7%; normalized EBITDA margin improved 498 bps QoQ to 44.4%
items.quote: As a result, our reported EB DAT margin expanded by 227 basis points sequentially to 41.7%. Importantly, adjusting for one -time items and IPL -related spend, normalized EB DAT margin improved by 498 basis points sequentially to 44.4%.

items.statement: Management expects margin expansion beyond 45% on broking & distribution over time, but will reinvest if growth opportunities arise
items.quote: think that there will be more margin expansion from here. I don't want to guide you on a specific number on that because at the same time, you should, of course, then we guide on someone, these things, it's on broking and distribution. But even in that business, if we get opportunities for growth, we will plough it back

items.statement: Commodity broking income grew 15.8% QoQ; F&O revenues up 16.1% QoQ; cash segment up 4.6% QoQ
items.quote: Within broking, we witnessed strong momentum in the commodities segment supported by a healthy rally in bullion and energy commodities , with commodity broking income growing 15.8% sequentially. Similarly, F&O revenues increased by 16.1% quarter-on-quarter, benefiting from elevated market activity and volatility during the quarter, while the cash segment registered 4.6% sequential growth.

items.statement: No change in credit distribution take rates; personal loan ATS not disclosed but no loans below ₹50,000
items.quote: Yes. So there is largely no change in take rate. But as we expand the book and as we get more lenders and the distribution of loans across lenders change, take rates can change. Having said that, our take rates are generally best in kind in the industry.

items.statement: Proposed capital infusion of up to ₹1.5 billion each into wealth management and NBFC platform to scale emerging businesses
items.quote: In this direction, the company has proposed a capital infusion of up to ₹1.5 billion each into our wealth management business and our NBFC platform, which will enable us to scale these businesses meaningfully and further diversify growth engines over the medium term.

items.statement: AI now embedded across platform: >50% of development augmented by AI; 80% of Ionic Wealth codebase AI-generated; Ask Angel evolved into conversational AI assistant
items.quote: During the quarter, we elevated Ask Angel into a conversational AI -driven assistant. It has evolved into a natural language interface supporting client service, query resolution, IPO discovery and stock insights.

items.statement: Employee count saw marginal decline QoQ; company continues to optimize headcount while filling critical roles
items.quote: Yes, I mean the employee count keeps on gyrating. There will be opportunities in the businesses where we will fill the gaps for critical hires and there will be instances where the bench strength that we have will fulfil the need for the business. So there is a marginal decline in the employee count quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Client funding book stable at ₹54.5 billion period-end; net worth ₹61.5 billion; cash & equivalents ₹165.6 billion
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain very strong with a period-end client funding book at ₹54.5 billion, net worth of ₹61.5 billion, and cash and cash equivalents of ₹165.6 billion, providing ample liquidity and financial flexibility to support growth while navigating regulatory developments.

items.statement: Elevated borrowings driven by YoY growth in client funding book, margin deployment with clearing corporations, and temporary liquidity arrangements for April 1 banking holiday
items.quote: The elevated borrowings on the balance sheet were largely driven by year -on-year growth in client funding book, margin deployment with CCs in line with elevated order volumes, and temporary liquidity arrangements undertaken to ensure uninterrupted operatio ns around the banking holiday on 1st of April 2026.

items.statement: RBI directions on banks' capital market exposures expected to have limited operational impact; funding ecosystem remains diversified via NBFCs, NCDs, CPs
items.quote: From a regulatory standpoint, the recent RBI directions relating to banks' capital market exposures are expected to have limited operational impact on us given our existing funding structures and collateral framework.

items.statement: Broking revenue share increased to 60.7% of gross income; distribution revenues moderated due to lower credit distribution and softer IPO activity
items.quote: The growth during the quarter was primarily driven by our core broking franchise with the share of broking revenues increasing to 60.7% of total gross income, highlighting improving trading activity across segments.

items.statement: Credit distribution penetration just starting: ~1 lakh customers took credit in last year vs 3.5-3.7 crore KYCs on broking side
items.quote: I think, just a flavour on the number of customers who have taken credit from us over the last one year is close to 1 lakh people. And we have 3.5 to 3.7 crores KYCs, right, on the broking side. So I think, hence the headroom for us for growth is immense.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost expected to remain in similar range; focus on gaining market share with higher quality clients
items.quote: On the cost of acquisition depends on a bunch of variables, channel mix, channel pricing, but more importantly on the tactical opportunities that we see to push for a larger mix of high value clients in that quarter or in that month, right? So it can go up and down a little bit. But I think more or less, we expect cost of acquisition to remain in the range of similar levels at this point of time..

items.statement: F&O premium market share grew 51 bps QoQ and 77 bps YoY; overall equity share up 46 bps YoY; commodity share up 100 bps QoQ
items.quote: When you look at the F&O premium market share, quarter-over-quarter we have grown by 51 bps and year-over-year we have grown by 77 bps. When you look at the overall eq uity market share where, when you add up cash and F&O premium, year-over-year we have grown 46 bps and quarter -over-quarter we're slightly down by 4 bps, mostly flat.

items.statement: One-time goodwill reimbursement of ₹192 million to clients due to external MII technical issue; engaging with MII for resolution
items.quote: Other operating expenses increased during the quarter due to higher client acquisitions, IPL -related brand investments, and a one-time reimbursement of ₹192 million to clients arising from an external market infrastructure disruption.

items.statement: No credit risk on distribution book (no FLDG); NBFC will start with loan against securities on own balance sheet
items.quote: Yes, in the distribution business there is no risk whatsoever on our books, no FLDG whatsoever.

items.statement: MTF book aging shows ~2/3 unwinds within 30 days; clients often bring own capital to unpledge rather than square off
items.quote: One, when you see the book unwinding, it's not necessarily that they square off the positions. Sometimes what happens is that at the time of the opportunity, clients may not have the full capital with them, and they are expecting some inflows over a period of time. And therefore, they kind of bring in their own capital and unpledge their stocks and retain those stocks in their portfolio.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to normalize to 25-26% of PBT as emerging businesses scale and deductions reduce
items.quote: But as the other businesses scale up and start making profit and the deductions reduce, the tax rate will come to about 25% to 26% of the PBT.

items.statement: IPL marketing spend for full season expected at ~₹1.5 billion, similar to past years; Q4 had lower booking due to late season start
items.quote: On the IPL costs, the overall cost that we will incur during the season and incidentally the season started pretty late in March, so there was a lower cost that got booked in quarter 4. But overall it will be about ₹1.5 billion, as we have been spending in the past as well.

items.statement: GST margin impact expected to be largely neutralized in FY27, tapering from ~110 bps in Q4 FY26
items.quote: On GST, the headwind on margins has been moderati ng in line with our guidance. The impact in Q4 was approximately 110 basis points, and we expect this to taper off further and be largely neutralized as we move into FY27

items.statement: FY26 VNB margin 24.2% post GST/SSV impact, down 140 bps YoY; ex-GST/SSV would be flat at 25.5%
items.quote: New business margins for FY26, excluding impact of GST and SSV, would have been flat at 25.5%. Post-GST and SSV impact, they were at 24.2%, a decline of 140 basis points versus FY25.

items.statement: Margin improvement levers intact: protection growth, rider attachment, non-par recovery, ULIP protection mix, lower fixed cost per policy, operating leverage
items.quote: Based on these factors, we expect margins to improve.

items.statement: Proprietary channels grew 15-16% in Q4 and FY26; 70%+ new customers first-time buyers; insured 46M lives in FY26
items.quote: However, our proprietary channels bucked the trend, delivering a healthy growth of 15% - 16% in quarter four as well as in FY26.

items.statement: FY26 individual APE mix: ULIP 44%, non-par 18%, par 25%, term 7%, annuity 5%; term up 200bps, annuity up ~300bps in Q4
items.quote: Our individual APE composition for FY26 was unit-linked at 44%, non-par savings at 18%, participating products at 25%, term at 7%, and annuity at 5%.

items.statement: Expect non-par savings to gain share in FY27 with supportive yield curve; protection and annuities to grow ahead of company average
items.quote: We anticipate non-par savings to gain share relative to FY26, with protection and annuities continuing to grow ahead of the company average.

items.statement: Launched AGNI variable annuity in Q4 FY26; annuity mix rose ~300bps YoY to ~8% of individual APE in Q4; margins higher than company average
items.quote: During quarter four, we launched Ajeevan Growth Nivesh and Income (AGNI), an industry-first variable annuity plan that combines lifelong guaranteed income with growth potential linked to the Nifty 50 Index.

items.statement: Embedded value INR 62,139 cr; operating RoEV 15.0% (15.4% normalized); PAT INR 1,910 cr (ex-GST/labour code +16%)

items.quote: We now open the floor for any questions you may have.

items.statement: Domestic supply chain for all components; no direct impact from global oil/gas or raw material inflation
items.quote: So, from the current situation, which is prevailing in the world. So, indirectly, everybody is impacted, actually, in one or the other form. But as far as the company is concerned, we are, we have all domestic orders and all domestic supply chains.

items.statement: FY26 revenue INR3,331.42 crore (+108.5% YoY), EBITDA INR641.10 crore (+106.2% YoY), PAT INR478.65 crore (+109.1% YoY)
items.quote: For the financial year 2026, we reported revenue of INR3,331.42 crores, a growth of 108.51% over FY2025. EBITDA stood at INR641.10 crores, up 106.21% year-on-year basis. While PAT reached INR478.65 crores, showing growth of 109.09% on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Cost to operate for Groww platform expected to increase in Q1 due to appraisals, then remain stable in absolute terms for rest of year
items.quote: With the exception of these risk related costs, I think you can assume that this will grow one in Q1. With the appraisal cycle, there will be a one-time kind of increase. And after that, we expect it to be kind of more or less stable for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Cost to operate for Groww platform will increase in Q1 due to appraisals then remain stable in absolute terms
items.quote: In absolute, it will increase in the Q1 because of the appraisals. And after that, in absolute, it will remain stable.

items.statement: Fisdom expected to be profitable by FY28
items.quote: I think in the shareholder letter you have called out that Fisdom should be profitable by FY28.

items.statement: Industry growth driven by bull runs; longer-term CAGR of 10-15%
items.quote: If you look at a longer frame the industry is growing like a 10% to 15% CAGR.

items.statement: New customer acquisition funnel shifted toward mutual funds and ETFs over last 1-1.5 years due to market conditions
items.quote: In last 1-1.5 years, the acquisition funnel has been slightly different primarily like you have seen that markets are not doing so great since September '24. Since then what we have saw that the acquisition funnel has shifted more towards mutual funds and ETFs as a product.

items.statement: Margin expansion correlated with revenue growth; expands if revenue grows >15%, more if >30%
items.quote: if our revenue grows beyond let's say 15% th en probably the margin will keep on expanding. If it grows 30% probably the expansion will be more. If it grows slightly lower, then the margin will not

items.statement: MTF book peaked around Jan/Feb end, dipped in March, current level post-dip; average likely similar or slightly higher
items.quote: We also saw a peak somewhere in between. I think probably Feb-end was or I don't remember actually Jan-end or Feb-end. We actually peaked and then there was a dip and this number is after the dip.

items.statement: MTF share of cash ADTO estimated between 5% to 10%
items.quote: My guess is it is still between 5% to 10%. It hasn't significantly changed.

items.statement: Marketing spend (cost to grow) largely fixed at INR 450-500 crores annually; Q1 slightly higher due to IPL
items.quote: If you look at between last year and this year we would have spent very similar to INR450 crores to INR500 crores is kind of spend.

items.statement: Headcount around 1,800; AI enabling more products with similar engineering strength
items.quote: So today the head count is around 1800.

items.statement: AI transforming software development lifecycle and customer support; launched GR1 co-pilot for customer research
items.quote: From productivity side, I think the entire SDLC, which is software development lifecycle, AI is kind of changing that completely, right, then from the overall like company operations perspective. And then on the customer experience side, our customer support, for example, and then we also launched GR1, is like a co-pilot customer can research and all.

items.statement: Launched commodities, bonds (primary and secondary), MTF scaled well; grew market share in equity, MF, F&O; entered wealth via Fisdom acquisition launching Fisdom, W, Prime
items.quote: We launched new products namely commodities and bonds, on bonds we had launched primary and now we are launching secondary. Billionbrains Garage Ventures Limited (Groww) April 20, 2026 Both the products have done well. We scaled some of the existing products, MTF scaled really well for us. In other products be it equity, MF, F&O we grew our market share. We forayed into wealth management with Fisd

items.statement: F&O penetration at ~10% vs ~18% pre-November 2024; ARPU recovered to pre-November levels due to MTF and commodities offsetting F&O decline
items.quote: The penetration of F&O is still in like 10% around range, which used to be like 18 odd percent before November.

items.statement: MTF primarily used by existing customers, not an acquisition product; most customers unique to Groww
items.quote: MTF for us is not an acquisition product. It is mostly our existing customers are using MTF. Earlier they might be doing intra-day instead of MTF is one use case where customers now are holding on to their positions for longer is one big use case.

items.statement: No significant industry shift seen from fee-only brokers; focus on per-transaction value proposition
items.quote: We'll keep a watch Samrith but as of now we don't see that.

items.statement: Waiting for regulatory clarity on algo trading before building scalable product
items.quote: We believe the new regulations that are still kind of getting cleaned up over a period of time will give us more clarity and we will probably jump into this market once we have full clarity on the regulatory piece.

items.statement: Settlement cycle quarterly for 10 years; no regulatory push to reduce further; customers prefer quarterly for convenience
items.quote: It has been quarterly since last 10 years now and I think it is again a choice. We haven't seen a customer being choosing bill to bill settlement significantly more than monthly or quarterly. Actually quarterly is probably what most customers want because it's a lot more convenient.

items.statement: Open interest limits not binding; average usage less than half of limit, no breach in last quarter
items.quote: On average we are like less than half of it on the limit side. And in the last quarter we haven't hit that limit at all for any day or any script.

items.statement: Risk-related costs from volatility in commodities (Feb) and equities (March Iran war) led to negative MTF balances accounted in cost to operate
items.quote: There is a risk related cost, which again, because of the volatility that we saw, both on the commodity side, and then on the equity side. So, Feb was more on commodity side when gold and silver kind of significantly moved in a day or two. And there was a square-off related kind of, you can say negative balances that people went in, and which we kind of accounted for in adjusted in cost to operate

items.statement: Wary of macro factors including tariffs and negative FII flows; not yet in clear positive cycle
items.quote: We are wary of lot of the macro economic factors that are impacting the market including tariff and including like largely FIIs being negative from the market has also impacted significantly the way market would have growth otherwise. I think we are waiting for that kind of clear signal to there where people have started FIIs have started putting money in India. I think that can be a good indictor

items.statement: AMC AUM grew 2.5x in one year
items.quote: Our AUM grew like 2.5x in one year and yes of course we became public so that was another milestone.

items.statement: Active internet population transacting online at 500-600 million and growing
items.quote: If you look at the active internet population who are transacting online and so on is in the order of 500 to 600 million and that is also growing.

items.statement: Investing in AI initiatives and wealth/AMC hiring driving employee cost increase
items.quote: On employee cost because we are investing across multiple functions including asset management and wealth side and there are initiatives on the AI side also that we are taking in Groww where we are doing investing. So this investment typically comes in the people form for us and hence the employee cost has increased a little bit from last quarter to this quarter.

items.statement: Stock advisory and MF advisory among highest requested features; will launch when right solution ready
items.quote: We have seen this demand for long now, like stock advisory, MF advisory. It's been quite, it's probably one of the highest asked questions in our voice of customer. And we have been kind of thinking about it. We will launch it when the timing is right, when we have the right solution and so on.

items.statement: Groww Prime available to some customers; will extend to existing customers when product meets high delta standard; no timeline given
items.quote: Prime, we have been kind of devising the product for some time now. It is available to some customers. And we feel that it will be in a position for existing customers. Again, we don't want to give the timeline, but we have some kind, we are optimistic about, we are optimistic about the creation of a product that our customers would love.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 1.5% to 3.5% YoY in constant currency
items.quote: Our revenue growth guidance for the financial year 2027 is 1.5% to 3.5% growth year -on-year in constant currency terms.

items.statement: FY27 operating margin guidance of 20% to 22%
items.quote: Our operating margin guidance for financial year '27 is 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Expect acceleration of growth in Financial Services and Energy, Utilities, Resources and Services verticals
items.quote: We expect acceleration of growth in F inancial Services and in E nergy, Utility, Resources and Services vertical.

items.statement: Full year large deal TCV of $14.9 bn, up 28% YoY; Q4 large deal TCV of $3.2 bn
items.quote: Large deals were very good, $14.9 bn for the full year, $3.2 bn for the fourth quarter. The full year was 28% higher than it was in the previous year.

items.statement: Net new component of large deals was 55% for the full year
items.quote: We see on the large deals, the net new is pretty large for the full year at 55%.

items.statement: FY26 operating margin at 21%; Q4 margin at 20.9%
items.quote: If you look at the margins, the full year margins is at 21%. The quarterly margins also 20.9%, very close to 21%.

items.statement: Q4 margin walk: -50 bps acquisition amortization, -30 bps one-off benefit reversal, -20 bps comp, +40 bps currency, +30 bps Maximus performance
items.quote: If you look at the puts and takes of the margin walk from the last quarter, we got 50 basis points impact from an acquisition-related amortization that we absorbed. There was a 30 basis points of one- off benefit that we got in Q3, so you know when you compare, that is a headwind. And 20 basis points was on account of comp-related matters. That was partially offset by 40 basis points of currency b

items.statement: FY27 margin headwinds include 60-70 bps from acquisition-related costs
items.quote: There is competitiveness in the market, there is acquisition that we have done. The acquisition related cost will impact margins by another 60 to 70 basis points.

items.statement: Stratus acquisition closed and baked into guidance contributing ~25 bps; Optimum acquisition and Australian JV pending regulatory approvals, not baked in
items.quote: The acquisition with an insurance company which is Stratus, which is already closed and it is baked in the guidance. What is baked into the guidance is approximately 25 basis points or a quarter point of the guidance. The other acquisition was Optimum, which is not baked in because we have not closed it yet. We are still awaiting certain regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Hired over 20,000 freshers in FY26; plan to hire at least 20,000 freshers in FY27
items.quote: The last year , we had announced 20,000 for FY26 and we have hired more than 20,000 freshers from the market. This year also , we are expecting at least 20,000 freshers to be hired.

items.statement: Headcount declined 8,000 sequentially in Q4 but grew 5,000 YoY for FY26
items.quote: So if you look at the headcount, our headcount sequentially has gone down by 8,000 employees but if you look at on a year -on-year basis it has still grown by 5,000.

items.statement: Wage hike quantum and timing not yet decided for FY27
items.quote: On the wage, we have not really made a decision at this point in time on the quantum and the timing of it. Once we decide we will let you know.

items.statement: AI services revenue growing nicely, higher than 5.5% of revenue reported in Q3, but exact number not disclosed
items.quote: No, it is growing. It is much more growth but we are not giving the number , but it is growing very nicely here.

items.statement: AI services across six areas (strategy engineering, data, process, legacy modernization, physical AI, trust) using Topaz Fabric and Cobalt platforms
items.quote: We see a large addressable market for AI services across the six areas that we mentioned - AI strategy engineering, data, process, legacy modernization, physical AI and trust. With our Topaz Fabric platform for AI and our Cobalt platform for cloud, we have differentiated capabilities that are operational today and that are working with our clients across each of these six areas of the AI landscape

items.statement: Strong growth in Financial Services, Communications, Manufacturing verticals and Europe geography in FY26
items.quote: We had strong growth in Financial Services, in Communications, in Manufacturing from the industry side and Europe on the geography side.

items.statement: Manufacturing vertical facing challenges, especially European auto; specific client wind-down baked into FY27 guidance
items.quote: Manufacturing per se is going through a challenging environment, especially the auto, in the European automobile sector. And within that we do have you know, certain headwinds from a particular client which will wind down towards the end of the year. That is baked in in the guidance right now.

items.statement: Pricing environment stable; FY26 growth was pricing-led as volumes were softer; AI revenue coming at better pricing
items.quote: In terms of pricing, I think pricing environment for us has remained stable. On the contrary, actually, most of our growth this year has been pricing-led because the volumes have been softer. And that in a way corroborates with the fact that the AI revenue are coming at a better pricing.

items.statement: Continued competitive intensity and AI productivity impact factored into FY27 guidance
items.quote: As we look ahead to the financial year 2027, we see large opportunities in AI services. We also see continued competitive intensity and we see an AI productivity impact, a combination of these things.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Iran war) created economic uncertainty; seeing paths to stabilization and underlying resilience in Western economies
items.quote: Now with the situation with the Iran war, there was a change in the economic environment. Now from what we are seeing, there seems to be paths towards things stabilizing. We hope everyone sort of gets there. From then what we understand like, just talking to people in the market and the clients is that, the underlying resilience of some of the economies where we have the big markets is pretty good

items.statement: Board actively overseeing AI strategy; Nandan Nilekini deeply involved in Topaz Fabric vision
items.quote: The Board is very active in our AI work looking at it and actually Nandan himself is very active because he is got a very good vision on where the AI is going and also helping like a lot of the Topaz Fabric what we have done you know he is working to give us the ideas.

items.statement: Acquisition pipeline strong; focus on strategic, cultural, value fit in areas like healthcare and insurance
items.quote: will continue to do acquisitions. There is a good pipeline. We did two which came like you know by coincidence like together, but in general we will continue to do acquisitions External Document © 2025 Infosys Limited 23 in areas like the healthcare which we did where we feel we can expand nicely and the market is good

items.statement: Contract discussions evolving toward outcome-based models due to AI transformation, but most contracts remain traditional
items.quote: There is lot of discussions now that can we look at some things because the AI is transformative, that can we look at something which is outcome based. We have built with our delivery leadership, with our sales leadership, good models or templates for how those are to be done and there are active discussions as it is still early times.

items.statement: Visa costs remained stable; H1B visas not filed in new regime
items.quote: No. So I mean visa cost for us has remained stable. We have not really increased our visa cost, the H1B visa in the new regime, we have not filed it. So our visa cost has remained stable.

items.statement: Over 90% of employees skilled on AI platforms; building forward deployed engineer teams for AI solutions
items.quote: So, both of those are getting developed quite rapidly and the skilling has gone on I think over 90% of our people -- yes about just over 90% of people are now getting skilled on different types of the AI platforms.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance 1.5% to 3.5% YoY in constant currency
items.quote: Our revenue growth guidance of financial year '27 is 1.5% to 3.5% year-on-year in constant currency terms.

items.statement: FY27 effective tax rate expected 29% to 30%
items.quote: We expect effective tax rates for the FY27 to be in the range of 29% to 30%.

items.statement: Client spending guarded with focus on cost optimization over growth-led transformation
items.quote: Client spending is guarded, with greater focus on cost optimization engagements as against growth-led transformation

items.statement: FY26 adjusted operating margin stable at 21% with currency and Maximus gains reinvested in talent, AI and sales
items.quote: Adjusted operating margin was stable at 21%. Gains from currency and Maximus were reinvested in talent, AI and sales and marketing.

items.statement: Q4 operating margin 20.9% down 0.3% sequentially adjusted for Labor Code impact
items.quote: Q4 operating margins stood at 20.9%, down 0.3% sequentially, adjusted for the Labor Code impact in Q3.

items.statement: FY27 margin guidance assumes wage hikes, productivity pass-throughs and AI investment offset by Project Maximus
items.quote: Our operating margins guidance for the year is 20% to 22%. This assumes headwinds from wage hikes, productivity pass-throughs and AI investment offset by initiatives under project Maximus.

items.statement: FY26 large deal TCV $15 bn with 55% net new, 28% YoY growth
items.quote: In FY26, we signed 96 large deals with TCV of $15 bn, 55% net new.

items.statement: Q4 large deal TCV $3.2 bn with 19 deals signed
items.quote: We signed 19 large deals during the quarter with TCV of $3.2 bn.

items.statement: Large deal pipeline remains strong
items.quote: Large deal pipeline continues to remain strong.

items.statement: Utilization excluding trainees 83% in Q4, 84.4% in FY26; including trainees 81.1% for FY26
items.quote: Utilization, excluding trainees , was 83% in Q4 and 84.4% in FY26. Utilization, including trainees, was at 81.1% for FY26 reflecting the investment made towards creating future capacity.

items.statement: Headcount over 328,000; voluntary attrition reduced 1.5% to 12.6% in FY26
items.quote: Headcount at the end of the year was over 328,000. Voluntary attrition reduced by 1.5% to 12.6% for the year , reflecting continued softness and our interventions toward talent retention.

items.statement: Onboarded 20,000+ freshers in FY26; expect similar hiring in FY27
items.quote: We onboarded more than 20,000 freshers in FY26 and expect to hire a similar number in FY27.

items.statement: DSO including unbilled net of unearned reduced to 78 days, lowest in seven years
items.quote: Strong focus on collections aided by technology interventions helped us reduce DSO , including unbilled net of unearned to 78, which is the lowest in seven years.

items.statement: Free cash flow adjusted for Labor Code and tax refunds $3.5 bn for FY26, $882 mn for Q4; adjusted FCF/net profit 106% FY26, 111% Q4
items.quote: Free cash flow adjusted for the Labor Code and income tax refunds stood at $3.5 bn for FY and $882 mn for Q4. Adjusted free cash as a percentage of net profit continue to be well above 100% at 106% for FY26 and 111% for Q4.

items.statement: Final dividend proposed INR 25 per share, total FY26 dividend INR 48 per share, up 11.6% YoY
items.quote: In line with our capital allocation policy, board has proposed a final dividend of INR25 per share which will result in a total dividend of INR48 per share, an increase of 11.6% over last year, once the final dividend is approved by the shareholders.

items.statement: FY26 growth led by realization increase from Project Maximus; volumes flattish
items.quote: Volumes for the year were flattish, growth was led by increase in realization thanks to Project Maximus.

items.statement: Productivity gains passed back to clients due to competitive intensity
items.quote: So Yogesh, market is competitive. As I said, the competitive intensity in the market has gone up and the productivity will get passed back to the client largely.

items.statement: AI services traction strong across six areas; Topaz Fabric and Cobalt platforms differentiated
items.quote: We see a large addressable market for AI services across six areas; AI strategy and engineering, data, process, legacy modernization, physical AI and trust. With our Topaz Fabric platform for AI, our Cobalt platform for cloud, we have differentiated capabilities to serve our clients across the six areas of AI.

items.statement: $50M+ clients up 3, $100M+ clients up 3, $400M+ clients up 2 in FY26
items.quote: Our $50 mn plus clients increased by 3 and $100 mn plus clients also increased by 3, $400 mn by 2 in FY 26.

items.statement: Strategic AI partner for 18 of top 20 Financial Services clients
items.quote: We are strategic AI partner for 18 out of the top 20 clients in this vertical.

items.statement: Competitive intensity increased; some competitors pricing outside model capabilities
items.quote: We have not seen in one or two quarters, the change that you referenced, though what we are seeing is that competitive intensity is pretty high. So every now and then, we see a competitor doing something which looks outside the range of what we think the models can do today.

items.statement: Manufacturing Europe client ramp-down and deal walk-away to reduce FY27 growth by 0.75% to 1%
items.quote: Reduction of 0.75% to 1% due to lower revenue from one of our large European manufacturing client. This was due to reduced client spend on account of challenging macro environment, along with our conscious decision to not pursue certain deal s that were not aligned to our return expectations.

items.statement: Target EM-LAP and embedded finance to reach 85% of total AUM by FY29
items.quote: The first , shift EM-LAP and embedded finance to 85% of total AUM by FY29.

items.statement: Target INR 220 crores annualized cost take-out by FY29
items.quote: Second, take out INR 220 crores of annualized costs.

items.statement: Run down Prime Intermediated portfolio at 15% to 20% annually
items.quote: Third run down Prime Intermediated portfolio at 15% to 20% annually.

items.statement: No incremental equity through FY29, growth funded from internal accruals
items.quote: The fourth no incremental equity through FY29, growth funded entirely from internal accruals.

items.statement: Target steady-state cash ROA of 3% to 3.5% by FY29 with negligible co-lending and DA income
items.quote: The fifth transition to be steady -state annuity -led, largely cash ROA of 3% to 3.5% by FY29, with negligible contribution from co-lending and direct assignment income.

items.statement: Focus verticals mix increased from 33% to 38% of total AUM in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The mix of focus verticals has moved from 33% to 38% of total AUM in a single quarter, the fastest quarterly shift on record.

items.statement: Emerging Market LAP AUM at INR 3,581 crores with GNPA 1.2% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Emerging Market LAP AUM was at INR 3,581 crores in Q4, with the GNPA of 1.2%.

items.statement: Embedded finance AUM reached INR 2,280 crores in Q4 FY26, growing 27% QoQ and 6x in 15 months
items.quote: AUM for this business has now reached INR 2,280 crores in Q4, growing 27% quarter -on-quarter, 6x growth in 15 months.

items.statement: Cost of borrowings improved to 10.16% in Q4 FY26, down 45 bps YoY for fifth consecutive quarter
items.quote: Our cost of borrowings came down to 10.16%; this is for the fifth consecutive quarterly improvement that we have shown. This was also down 45 bps year -over-year.

items.statement: Each 25 bps reduction in cost of borrowings worth INR 35-40 crores annualized at current AUM
items.quote: Each 25-bps point reduction at the current AUM scale is worth INR 35 crores to INR 40 crores annualized.

items.statement: Consolidated opex base of UGRO and Profectus was ~INR 750 crores last year, will reduce to INR 490 crores plus in FY27
items.quote: On the cost program, the consolidated opex base of UGRO and Profectus combined was approximately INR750 crores last year. This will reduce to INR 490 crores plus in FY27.

items.statement: GNPA at 2.5%, NNPA at 1.6%, coverage 45%, Stage 1 at 93.1%, collection efficiency 98% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: On asset quality, GNPA stands at 2.5% and net NPA at 1.6%. We had a good coverage over the GNPA assets at 45%. Our Stage 1 is at 93.1% of the overall AUM and collection efficiency stands at 98%.

items.statement: GNPA increase from 2.2% to 2.5% is denominator effect from non-focus book run-down, not incremental deterioration
items.quote: The move from 2.2% to 2.5% GNPA is a denominator effect as the non-focus book runs down; it is essentially not a deterioration in the incremental portfolio.

items.statement: Embedded finance GNPA at 1.7%, well within underwriting expectations of 4-4.5%
items.quote: GNPA is 1.7%, which is well within our underwriting expectations.

items.statement: Credit cost at 1.9% of average AUM annualized in Q4 FY26, expected to stabilize at little less than 2% for next two years
items.quote: Credit cost was at INR 72 crores, 1.9% of average AUM annualized, and this is well within the expected range that we intend to work on.

items.statement: Debt at INR 10,782 crores, well-diversified across banks, DFIs, and debt capital markets
items.quote: Our debt stands at INR 10,782 crores, which is well-diversified across banks, DFIs, and the debt capital market.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 21.2%, leverage 3.7x, no incremental equity needed through FY29
items.quote: We are standing at a healthy capital adequacy of 21.2%, which is up from 20.8% which we had shown last quarter. Our net worth stands at INR 2,906 crores with a very healthy leverage of 3.7x.

items.statement: Vintage EM-LAP branches (>12 months) producing INR 68 lakhs/month disbursements, targeting INR 80 lakhs/month
items.quote: Vintage branches, which are older than 12 months, are producing INR 68 lakhs per month in disbursements, approaching the management target of about INR 80 lakhs per month.

items.statement: EM-LAP branch network expanded to 317 branches across 13 states from 127 in FY24
items.quote: The Emerging Market LAP build-out is also complete - 317 branches across 13 states, up from 127 in FY24.

items.statement: Embedded finance active merchant customers at ~2.5 lakhs, yields 24-26%, average ticket INR 1 lakh, tenor 1 year
items.quote: Active merchant customers stand at approximately 2.5 lakhs. Yields for this segment are around 24% to 26%.

items.statement: Secured portfolio 67% of total AUM (GNPA ~1.5%), embedded finance ~15% (GNPA 1.7%), discontinued products ~3.2% GNPA
items.quote: Our total secured portfolio which I am including Machinery Loans also because they behave similarly is about 67% of the total portfolio, and the GNPAs there are in the range of about 1.5%.

items.statement: Unsecured loans (including embedded finance) to be maintained at 30-35% of total portfolio
items.quote: Our broad philosophy is that unsecured loans, whether they are unsecured business loans or embedded finance, should not go beyond 30 %-35% of the total portfolio.

items.statement: EM-LAP targets micro-SMEs with turnover <INR 3 crores (median INR 1 crore), ticket INR 7.5-50 lakhs, secured by property
items.quote: So, in emerging markets business, we are catering to customers who are micro -SME, typically with turnover less than INR 3 crores, median turnover of about INR 1 crores. We do only secured loans there with ticket sizes between INR 7.5 lakhs to INR 50 lakhs.

items.statement: Embedded finance targets small retailers with turnover INR 15-20 lakhs+, avg ticket INR 1 lakh (up to 5 lakhs), daily EMI, 1 year tenor
items.quote: On embedded finance, the target segment are small retailers with turnover range between INR 15 lakhs, INR 20 lakhs to a little higher. These are all retailers who are using some kind of payment ecosystem QR codes.

items.statement: EM-LAP branch network (318 branches) in top quartile among peers, built in 3 years vs 8-10 years for peers
items.quote: If you see and if you compare us with other larger players, we would be in the top quartile as far as number of branches are concerned.

items.statement: ECBs fully hedged for currency and interest rates, landed cost ~9.5-10%, pursuing more ECBs for cost and ALM benefits
items.quote: All the ECBs that we take are completely hedged for currency and interest rates. So, the rate that falls to us is completely landed in INR.

items.statement: Global macro uncertainty (geopolitical, trade policy) but UGRO's chosen segments driven by structural domestic credit gap of INR 30 lakh crores
items.quote: The global environment is genuinely uncertain: geopolitical tension, trade policy shift, risk appetite re calibrating. India is not fully insulated. And yet I'm more confident in UGRO's trajectory today th an at any point in our history.

items.statement: Aspires to double PAT again in FY27
items.quote: Last year, we doubled our PAT. We aspire to do that again in FY '27.

items.statement: Topline growth in FY27 similar to FY26; no abnormal growth due to high utilization
items.quote: Top line, I think growth will be similar to what we did last year. Again, what we did in Q4 and at similar capacity utilizations, there will be top line growth. And however, there cannot be abnormal growth on the top line because capacity utilizations already in the March quarter are high.

items.statement: Cumulative renewable energy benefit of INR50-60 cr annually to EBITDA once fully commissioned
items.quote: I think the cumulative benefits to the EBITDA once everything is commissioned would be about INR50 to INR60 crores annually.

items.statement: Aims to maintain or improve margins from Q4 levels in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So definitely we would like to maintain the margins. And see, very short term, very difficult to say anything because with so many uncertainties around in the world. So difficult to give an exact number. But yes, I think we should be able to maintain or better our margins from the March quarter for sure.

items.statement: Committed ~INR200 cr on renewable energy (INR150-160 cr capex + INR30-35 cr equity for PPAs)
items.quote: See, the capex on the renewal that we've already announced is roughly around INR150 crores, INR160 crores. And then there are some PPAs where we'll have some equity infusions. So that is another INR30 crores, INR35 crores. So, about INR200 crores is something we've already committed on the renewable side.

items.statement: New capacity capex under discussion; benefits not expected in FY27
items.quote: As far as any kind of new capex or further numbers are concerned, as I mentioned earlier, we are still working on that. So, we are working on what kind of strategy we want to move forward. So, it will be a two -year cycle for the new capex that we want to plan. So, I do not really have anything concrete to say on that today.

items.statement: High utilization across all segments; next growth leg requires new investment
