items.statement: FY26 large deal wins at $855 Mn, up 40% YoY
items.quote: Our FY26 total large deal wins came up at $855 Mn, up 40% over the previous year

items.statement: Q4FY26 large deal TCV at $182 Mn, average $200 Mn across 6 consecutive quarters
items.quote: Our large deal win continued its momentum with a healthy TCV of $182 Mn in the quarter

items.statement: Mobility segment showing early signs of growth, expect sustained momentum in CY26
items.quote: In summary, the Mobility segment is showing early signs of growth. We expect sustained momentum in CY26, driven by a robust pipeline and stronger deal ramp-ups of the large deals.

items.statement: Sustainability segment growth momentum to continue across Industrial and Plant Engineering
items.quote: We expect the growth momentum to continue for Sustainability segment across both Industrial and Plant on the back of ramp-up in large deals and strong pipeline.

items.statement: Tech segment recalibrated for profitable growth, expect growth from next quarter
items.quote: And we do believe that next quarter onwards, we should start seeing that growth again.

items.statement: Investing heavily in AI stack, tools, alliances and talent for Engineering Intelligence pivot
items.quote: So, we are going to invest heavily in uplifting not just talent also building tools, bringing alliances which can actually help us deliver this.

items.statement: Headcount increased by 522 to 23,830; expect to add another 500 in Q1-Q3 FY27
items.quote: We do expect to add another 500 sometime in Q1FY27, Q2 FY27, Q3 FY27 as well.

items.statement: FY26 Free Cash Flow at ₹1,280 crores, 100% of net income
items.quote: In FY26, Free Cash Flow came in at ₹ 1,280 crores. Our FY26 FCF as a percentage of net income stood at 100%.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of ₹40 per share, total FY26 dividend ₹58 per share, payout ratio 48%
items.quote: The Board today recommended a final dividend of ₹ 40 per share, taking the total dividend for FY26 to ₹ 58 per share. This translates to a dividend payout ratio of 48% for FY26.

items.statement: Leadership reorganization: Alind Saxena to drive strategic initiatives and large deals; Subrat Tripathy promoted to CGO Sustainability; Srinath Nagarur promoted to CGO Mobility and MedTech
items.quote: Additionally, Alind Saxena, who is currently Executive Director and President for Mobility and Tech, will take responsibility for strategic initiatives, large deals and growth markets.

items.statement: Rajeev Gupta elevated to Executive Director and CFO on Board; Amitabh Kant appointed as Independent Director
items.quote: I would like to congratulate and welcome our CFO, Rajeev Gupta, as Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer on the Board of LTTS. I would also like to extend a warm welcome to Mr. Amitabh Kant on his appointment as an Independent Director on the Board of LTTS.

items.statement: Less than 50% of revenue from 6 technology bets today; expect >70% in 5 years
items.quote: So Dipesh, to answer your question here, less than 50% of the revenue today comes from these bets. In 5 years' time, we expect more than 70% of business to be coming from these 6 bets.

items.statement: Gross margins improved 150 bps sequentially in Q4FY26 across all 3 segments
items.quote: Our focus on improving the quality of revenue and operational efficiencies has further boosted the gross margins in Q4 FY26 with a 150 basis points increase on a sequential basis. All 3 segments have shown sequential improvement in gross margins

items.statement: Effective Tax Rate for Q4 at 26.6%, FY26 at 26.5%; expect 26.5%-27% range going forward
items.quote: Effective Tax Rate (ETR) for the quarter came in at 26.6%. For the year, ETR was at 26.5%, showing an improvement of 90 bps over previous year. Going ahead, we expect this to be in the range of 26.5% to 27%.

items.statement: SWC business divested; classified as discontinued operations from Q4FY26; restructuring complete
items.quote: In March of 2026, we announced the disinvestment of SWC business. Accordingly, SWC business has now been classified as discontinued operations beginning quarter 4 FY26.

items.statement: Total ARR AUM increased to Rs 311,940 crore, up 26% YoY; Wealth ARR AUM at Rs 216,000 crore and Asset Management ARR AUM at Rs 95,000 crore
items.quote: Our total ARR AUM increased to 311,940 crores, up 26% year-on-year, with Wealth ARR AUM at 2,16,000 crores and Asset Management ARR AUM at 95,000 crores.

items.statement: Targets 12-15% of opening AUM as annual net flows on Wealth Management side
items.quote: On the Wealth Management side, we really strongly believe we should be able to get to 12-15% of our opening AUM every year as net flows.

items.statement: Expects Wealth Management AUM to grow 20-25%, relationship managers by 25-30% annually, and profits by 15-25% over next 3-4 years
items.quote: And continued with an opening AUM growth of 12-14%, we should be able to grow our AUM on the Wealth Management side by 20-25%, grow our relationship managers carefully by 25-30% every year over the next 3 to 4 years, and effectively grow our profits on the Wealth Management side by 15-25%.

items.statement: Revised quarterly TBR run-rate guidance to Rs 175-180 crore from earlier Rs 125-130 crore; aims to grow towards north of Rs 200 crore
items.quote: So, overall, I would like to say, together with the BNK Capital acquisition and 360 ONE Capital coming into place, it would be safe to say that 125-130 crores of quarterly TBR now today looks like closer to the 175-180 crores of TBR for sure.

items.statement: FY26 cost-to-income at 49.9%; core UHNI Wealth and Asset Management cost-to-income stable at 44-45%; targets consolidated cost-to-income of 45-47% over 2-3 years
items.quote: FY26 cost-to-income stood at 49.9%. However, cost-to-total operating income stood at around 50%, as against 49.5% during the previous quarter. The UHNI Wealth and Asset Management cost-to-income ratios remain stable at 44-45%.

items.statement: CEO expects core business cost-to-income in 44-46% zip code; sees operating leverage from maturing teams and new business scaling
items.quote: I think our cost -to-income remains in the region of the zip code of 44%, 45%, 46%, which is a superb number. And I think as we've seen a little bit of churn of teams, as well as additional new teams, and there's a passage of time where the older teams have become more productive and the newer teams are kind of getting to be productive, I think that model for us is v ery well solved

items.statement: Client portfolios diversified: 40-50% listed equities, 20-25% yield assets, 5% international, 5-10% safe debt, 10-15% alternates (real assets, private credit, private equity)
items.quote: Today, if I reflect and look back at our clien t portfolios over the last 24 to 36 months, they have been steadfast, largely because of a diversified allocation of not more than 40 -50% in listed equities, nearly 20 -25% allocation to yield assets, nearly 5% allocation to international assets, 5 -10% to s afe debt and 10-15% to alternates through a combination of real assets, private credit as wel

items.statement: HNI Reserve program has ~60 RMs across 12 locations managing ~Rs 4,000 crore AUM for 650+ clients at ~90 bps ARR retention
items.quote: On the HNI segment, our reserve program now has approximately 60 relationship managers across 12 locations, managing close to Rs. 4,000 crores of AUM for 650-plus clients at ARR retention yields of around 90 basis points.

items.statement: B&K Securities (now 360 ONE Capital) integration complete; FY26 revenue ~Rs 220-250 crore, PBT ~Rs 105-110 crore; added 6-7% growth from corporate treasury integration and equity market share gains
items.quote: B&K numbers have been very steady for the last 10 months as compared to the year previous to that. I think broadly speaking, we had a 220-250 crore top line in the previous year. We've been broadly around that range. In fact, added around about 6-7%, largely driven by early integration on the corporate treasury platform.

items.statement: ARR revenue Rs 2,289 crore (+34.5% YoY), 75% of total revenue; Q4 ARR revenue Rs 605 crore (+20.4% YoY); ARR retention 78 bps (Wealth 76 bps, AM 83 bps)
items.quote: FY26 ARR revenue stood at 2,289 crores, up 34.5% year-over-year, and ARR revenue now comprising 75% of total revenue from operations. Q4 FY26 ARR revenue was at 605 crores, up 20.4% year-over-year. ARR retention was at 78 basis points, with Wealth at 76 basis points and Asset Management at 83 basis points.

items.statement: Transaction & Broking revenue Rs 777 crore (+4.4% YoY); Q4 TBR Rs 230 crore (+53.7% YoY) boosted by full quarter consolidation of 360 ONE Capital
items.quote: Transaction and Broking revenues rose 4.4% to 777 crores for the full year and Rs. 230 crores for Q4, up 53.7% year-over-year. The strong Q4 numbers partly reflect the full quarter consolidation of 360 ONE Capital, the institutional equities business, formerly known as B&K Securities.

items.statement: Lending book (loan against shares, collateralized at 2x) has zero NPA and zero loss since 2016; margin funding book < Rs 50-60 crore; no stress seen in Q4 volatility
items.quote: On our lending book, which is largely a loan against shares book, which is collateralized at 2 times, typically on a diversified portfolio, we've not, fortunately, seen any stress at all.

items.statement: Received tax demand order of Rs 336 crore; believes all liabilities discharged, has adequate legal grounds, expects no material impact; will appeal entire order
items.quote: As an update to our past communication on tax-related matters, we have received an order today from the tax authorities with an aggregate demand of Rs. 336 crores. We believe that we have duly discharged all tax liabilities as applicable. We have adequate factual and legal grounds to substantiate our position, and we do not expect any material impact on the financials or on our operations due to t

items.statement: Board approved first interim dividend of Rs 6 per share for FY26
items.quote: The Board has approved the first interim dividend of Rs. 6 per share, continuing our disciplined capital allocation philosophy, returning capital to shareholders, where we have surplus, while retaining sufficient capacity to fund growth in our Lending, Alternate, and strategic initiatives.

items.statement: Equity and equity-related income (ex-banking) could nearly double over next 3-4 years from historical Rs 85-90 crore/year; TBR run-rate 160-180 crore/quarter currently
items.quote: And the 175-200 crore number is not something which is like cast in stone immediately. But I think to a number which was 125-140 comparable earlier, I think the 160-180 seems better right now.

items.statement: Carry income modelling: ~10 bps of carryable AUM (~Rs 30,000-35,000 crore) annually; bad year 5-7 bps (Rs 150-175 crore), good year 12-15 bps (Rs 300-325 crore); Alternates yield ~95-100 bps (mgmt fee 85-90 bps + carry ~10 bps)
items.quote: So, from a modelling perspective, I would say approximately 10 basis points is the right number to look at. And obviously, we've got about 85 -90 basis points coming out of the management fees on t he Alternates business. So about 95 -100 basis points on Alternates is the yield I would look at

items.statement: DPMS net outflow of Rs 212 crore in Q4 (ex-MTM) driven by corporate treasuries, not UHNI or HNI clients
items.quote: It's Corporate Treasuries, which has contributed to the negative number this quarter.

items.statement: Execution risk is biggest risk; managing 1,800 professionals, investing in middle management leadership depth, professionalizing organization, preparing for 2-4% annual attrition
items.quote: First and most important, I think the bigge st risk in India, and that's also the biggest opportunity, is at all points of time, we need to roll up our sleeves and handle execution, and that's most important

items.statement: B&K Capital equities retention ~5-6 bps; mutual fund yield compression from 1 April impact ~2-3% on ~Rs 200-225 crore base; synergy benefits more than offset the change
items.quote: On the Capital side, on an average, the B&K business was operating in the zip code of the 5 to 6 basis points retention. So, while there is a little bit of an impact, it's not an impact which is very large for us to kind of dramatically change our quarterly numbers. I think it changes by around about 2-3%.

items.statement: TBR split roughly one-third each: listed equity & related (30-35%, Rs 60-80 crore, half from PE/IB/M&A), fixed income & yield plus & real estate (~one-third), private equity/unlisted (~one-third)
items.quote: I think broadly about 30-35%, 60 to 80 crores, comes from largely a combination of listed and listed related equity. Half of that largely coming from private equity, investment banking, M&A activities. And around about a third comes from largely fixed income and fixed income yield plus and real estate.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 order intake over $208 million with book-to-bill ratio of 1.5x
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we secured an order intake of over $208 million for the year, resulting in a robust book-to-bill ratio of 1.5x.

items.statement: Record order book of INR24,166 million at end of FY26, up INR5,105 million year-on-year
items.quote: We've closed the FY '26 with a record order book of INR24,166 million, which is INR5,105 million higher than last year.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 normalized EBITDA margin at 10.3%, up 77 bps year-on-year
items.quote: Normalized EBITDA stands at 10.3%, 77 bps higher year -on-year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 11.7%, PAT margin at 6.1%, both highest of the year
items.quote: At a margin level, EBITDA improved 11.7% and PAT stood at 6.1%. Both EBITDA and PAT margin are the highest compared to all previous quarters of the year.

items.statement: No revenue guidance given for FY27; management confident of year-on-year growth in all four quarters
items.quote: FY '27, I think the revenue, I think we are not giving any other guidance right now on the revenue side, but we definitely -- I mean whatever FY '26 has gone by. So that is a year which was not a good year for us. I think now FY '27, you'll be starting seeing the growth, year-over-year growth we'll be seeing it in all the quarters, four quarters, which is a very strong.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining double-digit EBITDA margins in FY27 with potential improvement from operating leverage
items.quote: Since the current order book continues to remain strong, and we are happy about it, we can say that we are confident of sustaining it. And if we have the top-up in terms of the growth, the operating leverage impact will start kicking in, and we can have something on top of this bit of it.

items.statement: Sales pipeline of approximately $0.5 billion currently being worked on for FY27 order intake
items.quote: I think we have a very good order pipeline right now, as I said, it is closer to $0.5 billion order pipeline, which we have today, the sales pipeline where the teams are working out to make those things as an order intake.

items.statement: IPO proceeds fully utilized and account closed as of March 2025
items.quote: As of March 2025, we have fully utilized the IPO proceeds in compliant to objects defined during the IPO. We are glad to report that the IPO proceeds are fully utilized and the account stands closed.

items.statement: Target net working capital of 100-120 days; currently elevated but improving with inventory reduction in Q4
items.quote: Our target is to reach about 100 to 120 in terms of the number of days, but we ha ve some distance to go. Maintaining what we call a profitable efficient operations and growing is always a challenge, but we continue to do it, and we continue to work on improving it

items.statement: Pre-ordered critical long-lead components for entire FY27 to mitigate supply chain disruptions
items.quote: We have already ordered the materials for a long -- for entire FY '27, particularly for the critical items, where there are long lead items we already placed the orders.

items.statement: Build-to-spec (B2S) revenue share increasing; first year of B2S contribution, profitable and exceeding expectations
items.quote: BTS is a long -term play. Last year, we did not have. This is the first year we are having it. For the first year, it has done well. And this will -- in terms of fructification to series o rder and volume production, it will have a couple of years down the line is where it will come up. But overall, we are very happy with the way the performance has come up. It's better than our expectations

items.statement: Added new synergy customer from Cyient DLM stand-alone to Altek; first PO received in Q4 FY26
items.quote: we also added one of the new customers, the synergy customer from t he Cyient DLM stand-alone side. Now they also just started working with Altek. We got the first PO there in the last quarter

items.statement: Book-to-bill ratio greater than 1.0 for each quarter of FY26, full year at 1.5x
items.quote: Each quarter, we had a book -to-bill ratio of g reater than 1, which ends up at being 1.5x for the full year

items.statement: Altek acquisition integration slower due to tariff overhang; cross-pollination benefits just starting on trial basis
items.quote: and the growth in Altek continues to have a bit of an overhang with respect to the tariff overhang still continues to be there. There's no clarity in terms of how -- which direction is going, which I think we are all aware of, okay? Overall, the synergy benefits in the cross-coordination, there's a little bit of slowness in it. Hopefully, things should settle down and then it will lead to it. And

items.statement: Continued hiring of sales leaders across geographies and verticals; more additions in process for FY27
items.quote: we're also adding a few more people, where we are in the process right now. And with all that , we are definitely seeing more order intake in Q3 and Q4 and beyond, yes, from all these new people coming in

items.statement: West Asia crisis caused supply chain disruptions delaying materials via Dubai/Doha routes; impacted Q4 revenue
items.quote: All the cargo comes either from Dubai or I just think Doha. So that's where I think we had a lot of challenges in getting the materials. It is not that our final goods are only for the customers there in the UAE region. Okay, it is not for that. It is basically for all the customers where we have got impacted because of not getting the materials on time.

items.statement: Memory component lead times extended; 60%+ revenue from exports amplifies geopolitical impact
items.quote: Also, 60-plus percent of our revenue comes from exports. And therefore, the geopolitics and the global issues have a disproportionate impact on us.

items.statement: Gross margin stable with only couple of basis points movement; volatility from product mix and supply chain disruptions
items.quote: Gross margin, no, it's not seen as a huge movement. A couple of basis point movement has happened. It's a reflection of product mix in terms of what we manufacture quarter-on-quarter. It's not going to be uniform right. That's point number one. And point number two, there are also near -term factors of what the supply chain and the disruption and a few things like that.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; focus on working capital improvement and cash conversion
items.quote: During the FY '26, we saw elevated working capital typical of a ramp-up in revenue moderation phase. As we move into Q4 and forward, we are seeing clearer signs of normalization, with sharper control on inventory, stable receivables and a healthier cash conversion cycle.

items.statement: Over 90% revenue from rest of world; expected to remain same in near term
items.quote: Geographically, the rest of the world continues to account for over 90% of the revenues driven by strong demand across four industries we operate. It is expected to remain same in the near term.

items.statement: Order intake growth in FY26 at or above competition levels (35-40%) after FY25 challenges
items.quote: If you look at our order intake increase, I mean, you mentioned competition at 35%, 40%. We are also at that percentage between FY '25 and '26.

items.statement: Defense revenue share declined 68% year-on-year due to large order completion in FY25
items.quote: Defense share is low and having year-on-year decline of 68% due to large order coming to an end in FY '25.

items.statement: PCBA remains largest product category at ~48% of revenue; Box Build share increasing
items.quote: From a product category standpoint, PCBA remains the largest contributor at around 48% of the revenues, reflecting its continued strength across industry segment. It's also encouraging to see the Box Build revenue share going up.

items.statement: Strong FY27 entry expected with order book visibility, pipeline maturity, and early ramps
items.quote: As we look ahead, I am particularly engaged by a strong entry into FY '27. The order book, the pipeline maturity, early ramps all gives us measured confidence as we go into the new financial year.

items.statement: Achieved highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT (112% of installed capacity) in FY26, surpassing previous record of 11.64 MMT in FY24
items.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 crude throughput was 2.93 MMT at 111% of installed capacity
items.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

items.statement: Achieved best ever fuel and loss of 7.73%, MBN of 69.8%, and EII of 84% in FY26
items.quote: CPCL achieved the best fuel and loss of 7.73%, best MBN of 69.8% and best EII of 84% in the current financial year '25-'26, surpassing our previous best records achieved in the last financial year.

items.statement: Highest ever distillate yield of 79.1% achieved in FY26, beating previous record of 77.6% in FY20
items.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

items.statement: Highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT in FY26, up from 404 TMT in FY24
items.quote: CPCL achieved highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT, overcoming previous record of 404 set in 2023 -'24.

items.statement: Core GRM for Q4 FY26 was $10.3/bbl
items.quote: 10.3 $/bbl would be the core GRM.

items.statement: Gross debt INR1,900 crore, net debt INR973 crore; debt-equity 0.18 gross, 0.09 net
items.value: INR1,900 crore gross, INR973 crore net
items.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores. If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

items.statement: Interim dividend INR8/share and final dividend INR54/share recommended, total INR62/share for FY26 (highest ever)
items.quote: During the year, for the first time, CPCL paid an interim dividend, and we are happy to announce that in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

items.statement: FY26 capex INR856 crore vs INR673 crore in FY25; LOBS Group 2&3 project INR1,600 crore and retail outlet project INR400 crore over 2-3 years; normal maintenance capex ~INR500 crore/year
items.value: INR2,000 crore (major projects) + INR500 crore/year maintenance
items.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years. Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

items.statement: LOBS Group 2&3 project will add 250 KTPA capacity for Group 2 and Group 3 lube base oils
items.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

items.statement: Niche value-added products (7-8% of volumes) contribute ~15% of margins; MTO production more than doubled, Hexane capacity doubled from 30 to 60 KTPA
items.quote: About 7% to 8% constitutes these kinds of niche products. And this 7% –8% is currently contributing around 15% of my margins. And if you take one product like, say, MTO, it has more than doubled in the last financial year that we are talking. And if you talk about Hexane, I have doubled my capacity.

items.statement: Forex loss ~INR200 crore in Q4 FY26 and ~INR350 crore for full FY26, booked in other expenses
items.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

items.statement: ~90-92% of products sold to IOCL at refinery transfer price (RTP) under long-term agreement
items.quote: No, our agreement, as you would be aware, close to about 90% of our product, mostly HSD, MS, goes to Indian Oil. We have a tie-up with them, we've a long-term agreement with them for selling. And the agreement is at RTP, that is refinery transfer price.

items.statement: Achieved 1st quartile in 7 indices of Solomon Benchmarking Study including energy intensity and operational availability; only 2nd refinery in India to achieve 1st quartile in energy parameters
items.quote: CPCL achieved the quartile 1 position in 7 indices of International Solomon Benchmarking Study, which includes energy intensity and operational availability. And in the country, this was the only second refinery where we moved to first quartile in energy

items.statement: Export not compulsory; optimize across domestic and export markets based on commercial merit; export duty part of realization but not higher than crack
items.quote: Export is not a compulsion to me. Export is one of the options available to me to optimize my margins and realization. So main products like HSD, MS we evaluate all available markets and realizations. And then whatever mix and combination is best profitable for the company, those kinds of things we do. So, for compulsion, we are not booking anything on export.

items.statement: FY27 mined metal production guided at 1,150 KTPA plus or minus 10 KT
items.quote: Looking into the year ahead, with a well-structured capex roadmap in place, we are confident in sustaining this strong performance in the year ahead with an expected mined metal production of 1,150 KTPA, plus or minus 10 KT, and a refined metal production of 1,100 KTPA, plus or minus 10 KT, with an expected refin ed silver production of 680 tons, plus or minus 10 tons

items.statement: FY27 zinc cost of production excluding royalty guided at $975 to $1,000 per ton
items.quote: For FY27, we have guided zinc cost of production excluding royalty at $975 to $1,000 per ton, reflecting prevailing global uncertainties.

items.statement: FY27 planned capital expenditure guided at $500 million to $600 million for growth projects
items.quote: Planned capital expenditure for FY27 is in the range of $500 million to $600 million towards announced growth projects.

items.statement: FY26 total capex was INR3,600 crores with growth capex of INR2,000 crores
items.value: INR3,600 crores total, INR2,000 crores growth
items.quote: Total capex was INR3,600 crores for the full year and growth capex was INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: 250 KTPA integrated zinc smelter at Debari progressing with site mobilization complete and detailed engineering largely finalized
items.quote: On the growth projects front, we are making steady progress for the 250,000 tons per annum integrated zinc smelter at Debari. Site mobilization is complete and detailed engineering is largely finalized.

items.statement: Plan to expand to 1 million ton smelter at single location in Rajasthan with commercial process ongoing and mill orders expected by June
items.quote: We plan to do that where we are putting the 250 KTPA smelter. That means in one location 1,000,000 ton smelter will come up. So that design has been finalized. Now the commercial process is going on. I see that another one month's time we should be able to place the order.

items.statement: Hot Acid Leaching process and fertilizer project commissioning expected in 2Q FY27
items.quote: Given its complexity as a first-of-its-kind project in India, commissioning is now expected in 2Q FY '27. The fertilizer project is also on track for commissioning in early 2Q FY '27.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at record 57.0%
items.quote: Quarterly EBITDA stood at record INR7,747 crores, up 61.0% Y-o-Y and 27.0% quarter-on-quarter, with industry-leading EBITDA margin of 57.0%.

items.statement: FY26 zinc cost of production at $959 per ton, lowest in five years and below guidance of $1,000 per ton
items.quote: On a full year basis, we delivered a five-year low cost of production at $959 per ton, well below our guidance of $1,000 per ton.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 zinc cost of production excluding royalty at $903 per ton, down 9.0% YoY and 4.0% QoQ
items.quote: On the cost front, despite a volati le geopolitical environment, we achieved the lowest quarterly zinc cost of production excluding royalty since underground transition at $903 per ton, reflecting a decline of 9.0% year -on-year and 4.0% quarter -on- quarter

items.statement: India GDP growth for FY27 expected at 6.4% to 6.9% supported by government capex and domestic consumption
items.quote: The country's GDP growth for FY 2027 is expected to remain resilient at around 6.4% to 6.9% supported by continued government capex, infrastructure push, a nd robust domestic

items.statement: Zinc demand stable supported by galvanization, lead by battery demand, silver structural deficit from solar and electronics
items.quote: While zinc demand remains stable supported by galvanization, lead continues to witness steady battery-driven demand, and silver stands out structurally with strong demand from solar and electronics driving a sustained deficit.

items.statement: Q4 zinc price averaged $3,241 per ton, lead averaged $1,931 per ton
items.quote: During the quarter, zinc prices touched a high of $3,487 per ton with an average of $3,241 per ton, while lead peaked at $2,040 per ton, averaging at $1,931 per ton.

items.statement: Silver prices normalized from peaks but medium-term outlook constructive due to energy transition demand
items.quote: While prices have normalized from peak levels, the medium-term outlook remains constructive, driven by structural demand from energy transition and limited supply growth.

items.statement: Q4 domestic coal usage at 64%, softened imported coal prices contributed to lower cost
items.quote: Key drivers included higher domestic coal usage at 64.0%, softened coal prices of imported ones, higher pro duction, and strong by - product realization along with the better mine grades

items.statement: FY27 renewable energy consumption targeted at 30% to 35%, up from 18% in FY26
items.quote: So FY26 we closed for the full year around 18% renewable energy and for the full year in FY'27, we should be between 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Natural gas shortage caused marginally higher cost of ~$11 per ton in Q4 but no production impact
items.quote: It is a marginally higher cost in the Q4, maybe around $11 per ton, but on the production point of view, no impact.

items.statement: Silver contributed 45% to overall profitability in FY26

items.statement: E-commerce revenue at MLL level exceeds INR1,000 crores annually

I think the largest names in the world in terms of supporting us from a cybersecurity angle. So we are on the job there. I think we are fully aligned to it, of the idea. There is a repeated audit of our own system to

items.statement: Projecting approximately 25% growth ahead with PAT margin improvement towards 9.9% to 10.5% range
items.quote: Based on current momentum, we are projecting approximately 25% growth ahead, alongside an improvement in PAT margin towards 9.9% to 10.5% range.

items.statement: Order book stands at more than ₹900 crore including Dubai operations providing revenue visibility for a couple of years
items.quote: Our order book as in March stands more than 900 crores, you know, including our Dubai operations, which you know, so which provides us strong revenue visibility for a couple of years.

items.statement: Hot lead pipeline of close to $200 million with offers in market being sanitized and validated
items.quote: I would rather shed light on the hot lead pipeline, right? Because we're currently dealing with close to, I would say, 200 million odd USD with offers in the market, right?

items.statement: Current pipeline of ₹900 crore intended to be delivered in next 18 to 24 months
items.quote: So, as we said, that 900 crores are the current pipeline, which we will intend, which we will deliver in next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Contribution margins at 43.8% vs 45.9% previous year; pressure from Africa projects and portfolio mix
items.quote: If we see at a non-contribution margins, they are at 43.8, they are s till healthy compared to previous year, which was around 45.9%.

items.statement: Target contribution margin ~45%, EBITDA margin 13-14%, PAT margin 9-11% internally
items.quote: At operating level, we continue to, you know, operating as in contribution margins, we will ideally do around 45%, and at EBITDA level, our target is to do around 13 to 14%, and PAT level will be between 9 to 11% is what our internal targets are.

items.statement: Three main factors impacted margins: capability enhancement (talent acquisition), RMC cost up ~33%, execution cost up ~43% due to remobilization
items.quote: One was capability enhancement, which focuses on talent acquisition. One was the RMC cost, which grew up by close to 33%, and the last was the execution cost, which was up to 43%, which increased due to the remobilization of the installation t eam amidst the geographical conditions

items.statement: Freight cost increases compensated by dollar-denominated revenue; RMC procured in India so main challenge is freight
items.quote: If you look at main RMC cost, we still procure it in India, so I think the challenges is more on the freight piece, so delivery and execution can get delayed, but the impact on cost could be very small, you know, which will get compensated with. We're rising dollar because most of the revenue is in dollar terms.

items.statement: Receivables risen to ₹204.34 crore; receivable management now strategic priority with sharper collection-led discipline
items.quote: However, our focus for the next four quarters remains firmly centred on cash and collection , while our liquidity position remains strong. The receivables have risen to ₹ 204.34 crore. Accordingly, receivable management is now a strategic operational priority with sharper collection-led discipline being implemented to ensure that scale is supported by strong cash conversion and healthier working c

items.statement: Dubai receivables ₹37 crore, Saudi receivables ₹61 crore; high due to Q4 heavy billing, expected to reduce in Q1-Q2
items.quote: Our Receivables in Dubai is 37 crores, whereas in Saudi it is around 61 crores. This is part in, you know, typically because of last heavy quarter billing.

items.statement: GCC localization through subsidiaries: 100% subsidiary in UAE (FTS), 100% in Saudi (Fabtech Saudi), JV in Saudi (Mark Maker 33.33%), investment in TSA (16%), FABL (49%)
items.quote: We have 100% subsidiary called FTS in UAE, 100% subsidiary in Saudi Arabia called Fabtech Saudi, we have 33.33% in Mark Maker, which becomes our process OSD, closed loop line division, our own in-house investment of 16% now in TSA, which allows us to offer water systems across all the pharmaceutical projects, and FABL with 49%, which allows us to be a approved vendor for Containment solutions.

items.statement: Bidding for pre-engineered buildings and civil infrastructure to control project timelines, reduce greenfield execution from 24-27 months by ~20%
items.quote: Where we used to be at 24 to 27 months per greenfield project, now we're able to reduce that by, let's say, 20%.

items.statement: Expansion in Kenya showing extraordinary momentum; Africa emerging as powerful long-term growth corridor
items.quote: At the same time, our expansion in Kenya has demonstrated extraordinarily momentum, reinforcing our belief that Africa can emerge as a powerful long-term strategy corridor for Fabtech.

items.statement: Animal health segment growing in Middle East, North Africa, Saudi; secured vaccine fill-finish facility and multiple medical device/formulation projects in veterinary sector
items.quote: The animal health segment in medical devices in veterinary fields of vaccines and general formulations has been growing across the region. And we were able to bag not one but multiple projects in the Middle East, North African and Saudi Arabian region, which allowed us to secure a vaccine fill finish facility and multiple medical device and finish formulation projects in the veterinary sector.

items.statement: No cancellation risk in current geopolitical environment; clients have positive cash flows and understand pharmaceutical independence need
items.quote: Fortunately enough, this situation has not arose yet, and we don't expect it to, because even clients and the nations understand that pharmaceutical independence is needed for situations like this.

items.statement: Billing currency always USD via LCs; may move to Euros depending on war situation; never local currency due to devaluation risk
items.quote: No, it's LC back payment terms always, and it's always in USD currently, which we are currently having discussions with our finance teams and leaders in the market and th e board. We may move to Euros depending on the situation with the war, obviously. But never in local currency, because, as you know, pharmaceutical emerging markets that we operate in, currencies can get devalued, dollar remains

items.statement: Order conversion rate improved to 11% and reaching 16-17% of hot leads; expect huge order booking in coming quarters
items.quote: In nutshell, looking at our conviction and commitment in last quarter, you know, in that disruptive environment, we can say that our conversion is now getting improved. It is now 11% and it is reaching and hitting to around 16 to 17 percent of the hot lead.

items.statement: Leadership transition to Executive Chairman structure for sharper strategy direction, governance alignment, and long-term oversight; management continues execution
items.quote: The transition to executive chairman should not be viewed as a return to the operation, but rather as a move towards sharper strategy direction, strong governance alignment, and bolder long -term oversight. Simply put, management will continue to drive execution, while the executive chairman structure will help ensure that Fabtech remains strategically aligned towards th e right market, right oppo

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions disrupted supply chains, impacted freight economics, introduced volatility; pressure on profitability during critical execution phase of last quarter
items.quote: This year, however, came with extraordinary challenges. Global geopolitical tensions and the regional conflicts disrupted supply chains, impacted freight economics, and introduced volatility across the key markets. These factors did exert pressure on profitability, particularly during the critical execution phase of the last quarter.

items.statement: Other income more than doubled to ₹21 crore: major component ₹12 crore forex income, ₹7 crore interest on FDs from IPO funds and lending facilities
items.quote: other income, the major component of 20 crores is around 12 crores of foreign income. Forex. So different exchange rate and the balance amount, 7 crores are from the interest fund on the FDs which we have parked from the IPO fund and the oth er FDs for our lending facilities

items.statement: Strategic market penetration in cost-effective markets like Africa increases volume but lowers margins; volume increase will balance margins in near future
items.quote: There were active strategi c calls that Fabtech has taken to focus on a market penetration strategy in cost-effective markets such as Africa as well. And we would be fair to say that this strategy has allowed us to win more projects and increase the order pipeline, also focus on internal margin development, which you will see in the quarters to come

items.statement: Regulatory compliance backbone: WHO, EU-GMP, USFDA, UKMHRA guidelines followed in design and execution across pharmaceutical emerging markets
items.quote: Therefore, WHO, EU -GMP, USFDA, or UKMHRA. These are the backbone regulatory guidelines that are followed by the Fabtech team, be it in design or in execution.

name: Canara HSBC Life Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: FY27 total AUM growth target ~25%
items.quote: We expect another year of approximately 25% growth in total AUM.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated profit growth target ~50%
items.quote: We expect consol profits to also grow at approximately 50%.

items.statement: FY27 exit RoAUM target ~2.5%
items.quote: We expect to exit FY27 with a return on AUM of approximately 2.5% versus the 2.1% we reported in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Legacy book to become irrelevant by H2 FY27
items.quote: If we are talking about Legacy book next year at this time, we would be very, very surprised. It will become irrelevant by the latter half of this year, by Q4 of this year, it should become kind of so small to be irrelevant.

items.statement: Total AUM grew 25% YoY to INR1,01,230 crores in FY26
items.quote: On a consol basis, AUM was up 25% year-on-year and we ended the year at INR1,01,230 crores.

items.statement: Growth AUM grew 33% YoY to INR98,423 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Growth AUM was collectively thus up 33% year-on-year to INR98,423 crores.

items.statement: Retail AUM grew 33% YoY to INR85,885 crores in FY26
items.quote: In FY26, it grew 33% year-on-year to INR85,885 crores.

items.statement: Wholesale 2.0 AUM grew 38% YoY to INR12,538 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: As at March 2026, the Wholesale 2.0 book stood at INR12,538 crores, which was a growth of about 38% year-on-year.

items.statement: Legacy book down 59% YoY to INR2,807 crores in FY26
items.quote: We have completed our AUM mix transition with the Legacy book down 59% year-on-year to INR2,807 crores versus the target of reducing it to INR3,000 crores to INR3,500 crores.

items.statement: Retail disbursements up 34% YoY to INR13,101 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Disbursements in retail recovered from a moderate Q3 and were up 34% year-on-year to INR13,101 crores.

items.statement: Micro loans AUM up 42% YoY to INR1,384 crores in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our micro loans AUM was up 42% year-on-year from a small base to INR1,384 crores.

items.statement: Customer franchise grew 22% YoY to 5.7 million in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our retail customer franchise grew by 22% year-on-year to 5.7 million.

items.statement: Opened 108 branches in Q4 FY26; total network 701
items.quote: In this quarter, we opened 26 full -service branches, which we have now rechristened as urban branches. In addition to these, we have also opened 22 gold loan branches and added 60 rural branches, which we earlier called microfinance branches. We have now t aken our rural network to 136 branches. In all, our total branch network has crossed 700 in this quarter and stands at 701

items.statement: Plan to open 180 more gold loan branches in FY27 to reach ~200
items.quote: We expect to open 180 more gold loan branches in FY 27 to take our gold loan branch count to approximately 200.

items.statement: Consolidated NIM expanded 20 bps QoQ to 6.5% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our consolidated level NIM expanded 20 bps quarter-on-quarter to 6.5%.

items.statement: Growth book NIM at 7% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: You will also see on this slide that the consol e NIM has been continuing to close the gap with our growth book NIM, which is 7%.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing declined 11 bps QoQ to 8.84% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Cost of borrowing during the quarter declined by 11 basis points on a Q-o-Q basis to 8.84%.

items.statement: AA+ rating may lower cost of borrowing by 50-80 bps over 3 years
items.quote: Domestic credit rating upgrade from AA to AA+ has the potential to lower our cost of borrowing by 50 to 80 basis points once we churn our current borrowing stack out and replace it with new borrowings.

items.statement: AA+ rating could lift steady-state ROEs by 3-4 percentage points
items.quote: All of this could lift steady-state ROEs by 3% to 4% percentage points.

items.statement: Retail opex to AUM fell 21 bps QoQ to 3.6% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: On opex, retail opex to AUM further came down by 21 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 3.6% per annum in quarter 4.

items.statement: Retail opex to AUM may fall further in FY27
items.quote: While we have restarted our branch expansion, the continued productivity gains for our employees and branches have the potential to take our retail opex to AUM a little bit lower than current levels over FY27.

items.statement: Retail 90+ DPD down 20 bps QoQ to 0.6% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The stability and predictability are also visible in our credit risk outcomes, with retail 90 plus delinquencies down 20 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 0.6%.

items.statement: Growth business credit cost down marginally QoQ to 1.5% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Growth business credit cost was also down marginally quarter-on-quarter to 1.5%.

items.statement: Consolidated GNPA and NNPA down 30 bps QoQ to 2.3% and 1.6% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our total GNPA and NNPA were down 30 bps quarter-on-quarter each to 2.3% and 1.6%, respectively.

items.statement: Wholesale 2.0 asset quality robust with zero NPAs
items.quote: Asset quality remained robust with zero NPAs in this book as Anand mentioned earlier.

items.statement: Micro loan portfolio almost completely normalized
items.quote: The micro loan portfolio has almost completely normalized, as you see in our 90 DPD chart that we share every quarter.

items.statement: Used car portfolio risk fell steeply in Q4 after three elevated quarters
items.quote: In our semi-secured business, which is used cars, after three quarters of elevated risk metrics, we saw a steep fall in Q4.

items.statement: Smaller ticket MSME mortgages stabilized and performing better
items.quote: Over this last quarter, however, we have seen this segment stabilize and perform noticeably better than before.

items.statement: Monitoring Middle East conflict impact on vulnerable sectors; bounce rates in April same as March
items.quote: Bounce rates in these vulnerable sectors in April have come in at the same levels as March.

items.statement: Tightened fresh underwriting in sectors sensitive to Iran conflict
items.quote: We have thus tightened fresh underwriting in these sensitive sectors.

items.statement: Average quarterly LCR 450% in Q4 FY26; cash and equivalents INR8,640 crores (8% of assets)
items.quote: Our average quarterly LCR in Q4 was 450%. We have cash and cash equivalents of INR8,640 crores, equivalent to 8% of all our assets.

items.statement: Incremental long-term borrowing cost 8.4%; short-term ~7.25%
items.quote: Our incremental borrowing cost for long-term money was 8.4%. We didn't raise much short-term at all, so I don't know, my guess would be that short-term will be like 7.25% right now if we went to the market and started raising short money.

items.statement: Received $148 million deferred proceeds from Piramal Imaging sale in Q4 FY26
items.quote: In Q4, we received deferred consideration proceeds of $148 million towards the sale of Piramal Imaging.

items.statement: Concluded Shriram Life Insurance stake sale worth INR600 crores
items.quote: We also concluded the stake sale of Shriram Life Insurance worth INR600 crores.

items.statement: Leverage (AUM/equity) increased to 3.6x in Q4 FY26 from 3x YoY; target 4.5-5x
items.quote: Leverage, which is AUM to equity, also continued to increase and we are now up at 3.6x in Q4 compared to 3x same quarter last year. We continue to progress towards our goal of 4.5 to 5x.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 19.8% as of March 2026
items.quote: Our capital adequacy is very strong at 19.8% as on March 2026.

items.statement: Accumulated tax losses INR24,600 crores; ~INR16,000 crores future profits tax-protected
items.quote: We also added INR10,110 crores to our assessed tax losses, totaling total assessed tax losses to INR24,600 crores.

items.statement: Interested in M&A in microfinance, gold loans, MSME at value pricing; nothing imminent
items.quote: We remain interested in the spaces of microfinance, gold loans, MSME, any of these spaces, you know, we remain interested and we do look at a lot of deals, but nothing's imminent.

items.statement: Operations productivity doubled in 2 years while headcount flat; AUM doubled
items.quote: You can see on this slide that operations productivity has doubled in the last 2 years. Our AUM has doubled in this period, whereas our operations staff and headcount has remained roughly flat.
